answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: that the readers outside artifact address only the head path, appending or reading recent entries, and none replays the whole file by itself. Six readers name the file by path: build_inspector/inspector.py, tester red_tickets.py and hollow.py, cc scripts prove.sh and close.sh, and the installer. D1 censuses them, and any whole-file replay is routed through artifact.read_journal, the tool's published reader. A second assumption: GitHub's limit is per file, so segments under the bound clear GH001 even though the repo keeps growing.
answers.builder_check: A builder needs: (a) read_journal and verify_chain at cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py:289 and :313, and the appender in the same file; (b) the bound K as a module constant, chosen so a segment stays well under 50 MB (measured 33 MB over 22895 entries, about 1.4 KB per entry, so K = 20000 gives about 28 MB); (c) the segment path, .artifact-journal/<NNNN>.jsonl beside the head, zero-padded and ordered by name; (d) the census of the six path readers (grep for .artifact-journal); (e) the proof fixture, a scratch root with K overridden small. All five are in the how and decisions.
answers.children: none, because the change is the appender, read_journal and verify_chain in cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py, plus a census of the path readers
answers.collision_check: 0f8aefbba1d0 (a journal line lands at the path even when git replaced it) holds the head path; unchanged. The merge driver b7d2e05a1c93 merges the head; unchanged unless a merge crosses a cut. Law 5 (history past right-now berths in the commons) is a distinction: the journal is a record of truth that verify_chain replays from genesis, not a working-surface history, so sealed segments stay beside it in the repo.
answers.falsifier_check: Clause 1: a scratch root whose journal passes the bound K is split on append into a sealed .artifact-journal/0001.jsonl and a head, each holding at most K entries, and verify_chain over the root returns no faults. Clause 2: a one-byte edit in the sealed segment makes verify_chain name the fault, and so does a head whose first prev does not equal the segment's last entry sha. Clause 3: read_journal returns every entry in order across segment and head. Horizon: the live cairn journal, on its next append past the bound, splits, and the next Dell push carries no GH001.
answers.gates_bound: code-seam@v2's prove gate: a red-first proof under cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/, hollow-sealed; feeds back to TICKETME/FIXME on failure (Laws 3 + 8).
answers.missing_check: The cut must be the same on every box. Boxes append concurrently and merge through the journal merge driver (b7d2e05a1c93), so a cut on the local file size would seal different bytes on different boxes and fork the segments. The cut is at a fixed entry count, counted from genesis: entry N*K closes segment N. The merge driver only touches the head, and a merge that crosses a cut is a case the proof must cover.
